questions.prompt: You created a Premium block blobs storage account. The team now wants the same account converted to Standard general-purpose v2 to use Azure Files. What must you do?
options: Change the account kind on the Configuration page
Create a new Standard general-purpose v2 account and copy the data to it
Run Set-AzStorageAccount -Kind StorageV2
Open a support request to convert it
questions.explanation: You can't change a storage account to a different type after it's created; create a new account and copy the data.
why_not: An account's type can't be changed after creation.
Type changes aren't supported, whatever the tool.
Microsoft documents that you must create a new account and copy the data.
questions.clue: "converted" from Premium to Standard GPv2: an account's type never changes, so create a new account and copy.

questions.prompt: Which storage account name is valid?
options: Contoso-Data
cd
contosodata2026
contoso_data_archive
questions.explanation: Storage account names are 3-24 characters of lowercase letters and numbers, and must be unique across Azure.
why_not: Only lowercase letters and numbers are allowed; no uppercase and no hyphens.
Names must be at least 3 characters.
Underscores aren't allowed.
questions.clue: Storage account naming: 3 to 24 characters, lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique.

questions.prompt: You need to move a storage account and its data from West Europe to North Europe. What is the supported approach?
options: Create a new account in North Europe and copy the data, for example with AzCopy
Use Move-AzResource with a new location
Change the account's location property
Enable GRS and fail over permanently
questions.explanation: Moving a storage account to another region means creating a copy of the account there and moving the data with AzCopy or another tool.
why_not: Resource moves change the resource group or subscription, never the region.
The region of an existing account can't be changed.
Failover goes to the paired region, which you can't choose; it isn't a move to an arbitrary region.
questions.clue: "from West Europe to North Europe": storage accounts don't move regions; copy to a new account.

questions.prompt: An application must keep reading blob data even during a regional outage, without anyone initiating a failover. Which redundancy option meets this at the lowest cost?
options: GRS
ZRS
RA-GZRS
RA-GRS
questions.explanation: Only the RA variants allow reads from the secondary region at any time. RA-GRS is cheaper than RA-GZRS.
why_not: GRS data in the secondary region isn't readable unless there's a failover.
ZRS stays within one region; a regional outage affects all three zones.
It meets the requirement but costs more than RA-GRS; zone redundancy wasn't requested.
questions.clue: "keep reading during a regional outage" and "without failover" at "lowest cost": RA-GRS.

questions.prompt: A storage account uses ZRS. You must change it to GRS. What is correct?
options: Select GRS on the Redundancy page; it converts immediately
There's no direct ZRS to GRS conversion; go through GZRS or LRS in two steps, waiting at least 24 hours between them
It's impossible; you must create a new account
Delete the zone copies with PowerShell first
questions.explanation: ZRS to GRS requires ZRS → GZRS → GRS or ZRS → LRS → GRS, with at least 24 hours between conversions.
why_not: ZRS to GRS isn't offered directly.
It's possible through an intermediate option.
There's no such operation; conversion is the supported path.
questions.clue: "ZRS to GRS": no direct path; it takes two conversions.

questions.prompt: You need zone redundancy for a Premium file shares account and also want geo-redundancy. What can you configure?
options: GZRS
RA-GZRS
ZRS only; Premium storage accounts support LRS and ZRS, not geo-redundant options
GRS with zone pinning
questions.explanation: Premium block blob, file share and page blob accounts support LRS and ZRS only.
why_not: Premium file shares accounts don't support GZRS.
Premium accounts don't support any geo-redundant option.
There's no such option; premium accounts support LRS or ZRS.
questions.clue: "Premium file shares" plus "geo-redundancy": Premium accounts support LRS and ZRS only.

questions.prompt: You're configuring object replication from account A to account B. Configuration fails. Which prerequisite is most likely missing?
options: Blob versioning on both accounts, or the change feed on account A
Hierarchical namespace on both accounts
GRS redundancy on account A
A stored access policy on the destination container
questions.explanation: Object replication requires blob versioning on the source and destination accounts, and the change feed on the source.
why_not: Object replication isn't supported on accounts with a hierarchical namespace.
Object replication doesn't depend on the redundancy option.
Stored access policies are for SAS tokens, not replication.
questions.clue: "object replication" configuration fails: versioning on both accounts, change feed on the source.

questions.prompt: Object replication has run for a week. A batch job that uploads to the destination container fails with 409, and blobs that were in the source before the policy aren't at the destination. What explains both?
options: The destination account needs the change feed
The batch job needs a user delegation SAS
Replication only runs once a day
The destination container is read-only while a rule targets it, and rules copy only new blobs by default
questions.explanation: Writes to a destination container fail with 409 while replication is active. Pre-existing blobs are ignored unless you choose to copy them.
why_not: The change feed is required on the source.
The failure is 409 Conflict from the rule, not authorization.
Replication is asynchronous and continuous; the defaults explain the missing blobs.
questions.clue: "uploads to the destination fail with 409" and old blobs missing: the destination is read-only, and only new writes replicate by default.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between GRS and object replication?
options: Object replication is synchronous; GRS is asynchronous
GRS copies the whole account to the paired region; object replication copies block blobs from chosen containers to an account you choose
GRS supports only block blobs
Object replication makes the source read-only
questions.explanation: Redundancy protects the whole account in its paired region. Object replication distributes selected block blobs to destinations you pick, in any region.
why_not: Both are asynchronous.
GRS covers the whole account, all data types; object replication supports block blobs only.
The destination container becomes read-only, not the source.
questions.clue: GRS copies the whole account to a Microsoft-chosen region; object replication copies chosen containers to an account you choose.

questions.prompt: Compliance requires that you control and rotate the key that protects a storage account's Blob and Files data. What should you configure?
options: Customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault with soft delete and purge protection, accessed by a managed identity
Infrastructure encryption
Customer-provided keys on every request
A key expiration policy on the access keys
questions.explanation: Customer-managed keys in Key Vault or Managed HSM protect Blob and Azure Files data. The vault needs soft delete and purge protection, and the identity needs get, wrapkey and unwrapkey.
why_not: It adds a second layer, but with Microsoft-managed keys.
That's for per-request Blob operations; it isn't account-wide key management and doesn't cover Azure Files.
Access keys authorize requests; they aren't the encryption key.
questions.clue: "control and rotate the key": customer-managed keys in Key Vault.

questions.prompt: An existing storage account must now have double encryption of data at rest. What must you do?
options: Enable infrastructure encryption on the Encryption page
Switch to customer-managed keys
Create a new storage account with infrastructure encryption enabled and move the data
Enable HTTPS-only transfer
questions.explanation: To doubly encrypt data, you must create an account or encryption scope that is configured for infrastructure encryption.
why_not: Infrastructure encryption must be enabled when the account is created.
CMK changes who manages the key; it doesn't add a second encryption layer.
That protects data in transit, not at rest.
questions.clue: "existing account" plus "double encryption": infrastructure encryption is a creation-time setting.

questions.prompt: One storage account holds data for two customers, and each customer's containers must be encrypted with a different key. What should you use?
options: Two access keys, key1 and key2
Object replication to two accounts
Infrastructure encryption
Encryption scopes, one per customer, set as the default scope on each customer's containers
questions.explanation: Encryption scopes let you manage encryption with a key scoped to a container or blob, which creates boundaries between customers in the same account.
why_not: Access keys authorize requests; they don't select encryption keys.
That copies data; it doesn't separate encryption keys within an account.
It uses a single Microsoft-managed key for the second layer.
questions.clue: "one storage account" and "different key per customer": encryption scopes.

questions.sub_skill: Manage data by using Azure Storage Explorer and AzCopy
questions.prompt: You must copy 500 GB between two storage accounts. The administrator's laptop has a slow connection. Which approach avoids sending the data through the laptop?
options: Download with Storage Explorer, then upload
azcopy copy from the source URL to the destination URL, which uses server-to-server APIs
azcopy sync from the laptop's local folder
Set up GRS on the source
questions.explanation: AzCopy uses server-to-server APIs when copying between accounts, so data moves directly between storage servers.
why_not: That routes all the data through the laptop.
That copies from local storage, so the data must be on the laptop first.
GRS replicates to the paired region's hidden secondary, not to another account.
questions.clue: "500 GB" and "slow laptop connection": a service-to-service copy between URLs.

questions.sub_skill: Manage data by using Azure Storage Explorer and AzCopy
questions.prompt: You own a storage account and run azcopy login, then azcopy copy to upload a file. It fails with 403. What is the most likely fix?
options: Run AzCopy as a local administrator
Regenerate the storage account keys
Assign yourself Storage Blob Data Contributor, or use a SAS token
Upgrade the account to Premium
questions.explanation: As an owner of a storage account you aren't automatically given data permissions. Uploads with Entra authorization need a role such as Storage Blob Data Contributor.
why_not: Local OS privileges don't affect Azure authorization.
Entra-authorized AzCopy doesn't use the keys.
Account performance tier doesn't affect authorization.
questions.clue: "own a storage account" but 403 on upload: owning the account isn't a data role.

questions.sub_skill: Manage data by using Azure Storage Explorer and AzCopy
questions.prompt: A container must always mirror a folder on a file server, in one direction only, transferring only changes on each run. Which command fits?
options: azcopy sync
azcopy copy
azcopy make
Object replication
questions.explanation: azcopy sync is one-way synchronisation between local storage and Blob Storage, or between containers.
why_not: copy transfers what you point it at on each run, rather than comparing source and destination.
make only creates a container or share.
Object replication copies between storage accounts, not from a file server.
